samples.summary: "Every CI run for the SHA must be green" has no supersession path, so one stale non-success run can make promotion permanently unsatisfiable
samples.evidence: `ciConclusion` returns "failure" unless EVERY matched run concluded `success`; any terminal non-success (`failure`, `cancelled`, `stale`, `action_required`, `skipped`) counts against the SHA forever. The old rule let a later run supersede an earlier one. `ci.yml` triggers on `pull_request` with default activity types, which includes `reopened`, so a closed→reopened PR gets a SECOND CI run against the SAME head SHA; if the first one is red or was cancelled, gate 1 can never be satisfied again for that SHA. The documented recovery path does not help: `agent-rerun.yml:186-190` lists runs with `per_page: 1` and re-runs only the newest, which cannot change the older run's conclusion, and `ci.yml` has no `concurrency:` block to collapse duplicates. The design note (docs/design/harness-engineering.md, "Every CI run for the SHA must be green") only reasons about the fail-open direction and does not consider a non-success run that no re-run can clear — cost is a promotable PR stuck as a draft with no in-pipeline way out.

samples.summary: Gate-1 semantics change goes past the originating task's explicit Non-goal ("No change to mark-ready.mjs's behavior")
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md:47-51 states the Non-goals: "No change to `mark-ready.mjs`'s behavior or its exit-code numbering… only the consumer and the tests change," and its Plan item for the CI filter is only mutant-killing ("deleting the `name === \"CI\"` workflow-run filter", line 44) — i.e. a TEST that pins the existing filter. This delta instead rewrites gate 1's behavior twice over (match by workflow path; require every run green), plus new `outcome` plumbing into loop-status. Both are behavior changes to the promotion gate the issue deferred, and they carry real promotion risk (see the no-supersession finding). If the hardening is wanted, it belongs to its own task doc with its own plan, not folded into the consumer-only follow-up.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the tree. The task doc's Non-goals (docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md:47-53) say "No change to `mark-ready.mjs`'s behavior or its exit-code numbering … only the consumer and the tests change", and its only gate-1 Plan item (line 43-44) is a mutant-killing test pinning the existing `name === "CI"` filter (the Verification list at 116-121 still treats that filter as live code). The delta nonetheless rewrites gate 1: `.trusted/scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:133-137` (main) filters by `r.name === "CI"` with newest-run-wins, whereas `scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:133-136` now calls `ciConclusion`, and `scripts/agent/checks.mjs:58-89` adds `CI_WORKFLOW_PATH`/`ciRunsFor`/`ciConclusion` (path matching + every-run-must-be-green + null-while-in-flight) — none of which exist in `.trusted/scripts/agent/checks.mjs`. The semantics change also propagates to a second reader via `scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:34,226-228`. That the same delta carries the #937 exit-code work is confirmed by the test file diff (`.trusted/.../mark-ready.test.mjs:243` old assertion vs `scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs:424-503` new `case`/`grep -qF` suite) and the workflow's new `case`/`outcome=` block (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1515-1572), so this is the #937 change and the quoted Non-goal governs it. The design doc was updated (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1904-1929), which softens the doc-discipline angle, but the scope-past-a-stated-Non-goal point is in-lane for design-fit and I have no named ground to refute it.
